prior_year_events.event_name: Prior year reserve re-estimation (2021 underwriting year)
prior_year_events.impact_description: Adverse movement in the 2021 underwriting year estimates versus the prior diagonal resulting in a gross strengthening of approximately 22.1m (based on the gross claims development table).

data.standardized_narrative: At 31 December 2023 the Syndicate carried gross claims outstanding of 786.531m (USD). Analysis of the claims development shows a net gross prior-year adverse movement (strengthening) of approximately 22.1m driven by movement in the 2021 underwriting year. The report also discloses net favourable movements of 27.6m after reinsurance recoveries; this net release is driven by favourable adjustments across several classes (notably third party liability and reinsurance lines) partially offset by adverse movement in Property (Fire). The presence of a large Reinsurance to Close (RITC) transfer in the year means the development tables and movements require careful interpretation.
raw_causal_phrases: This change reflects two primary factors: a decrease in large catastrophe losses compared to the previous year, leading to improved gross loss ratios, and positive adjustments to prior year claims across most lines of business.
Reinsurance recoveries were however lower due to the absence of major catastrophe events.

Favourable movements of $27.6m (2022: $34.4m favourable) in the past year's provision for claims outstanding, net of expected reinsurance recoveries, are included in claims incurred, net of reinsurance.
data.data_quality_notes: Gross prior year development derived from the gross claims development table (triangle). The report also discloses a net favourable movement of $27.6m (net of reinsurance). A large Reinsurance to Close (External RITC) transfer relating to 2020 and prior years was processed on 1 January 2023 (noted in Technical Provisions) which can distort development patterns; this reduces confidence in triangle-based gross PYD. Gross PYD therefore reported with moderate confidence.
